content_of_post_to_comment: We’ve all heard that God created a perfect world that fell into chaos and disorder as a result of human sin. But I’m not sure the Bible teaches that the world was created perfect. God created a good world, but he commissioned humanity as his regents to participate in the work of perfecting creation. I suspect that, even if humankind had never fallen into sin, the Son would still have become incarnate to bring this work to its fulfillment.
comment: The distinction between a good and a perfect creation raises an intriguing question: is redemption only a response to failure, or also the completion of a divine intention that was always moving creation toward communion?
